analysis:
The two supplied units are base_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 1629-2117). They contain only historical release notes (v0.9.1 through v0.9.8 App Attest, prefix-cache and related items) and no executable code. The patch excerpt shows the PR changes only CHANGELOG.md, replacing the v0.10.1 candidate header with a v0.10.2 candidate section at head lines 11-246. The visible patch portion is documentation about rollout, logprobs gating, cache-routing allowlist, and 4-bit SSD checkpoints for Nemotron 3.5 Super and GLM-5.3-Flash. It introduces no code, configuration, or control changes.

Security-relevant claims in the visible patch text, relevant to T-041 (prefix cache, SEC-035) and the coordinator-authored cache scope:
- It says cache routing is gated by an allowlist of (model_id, model_aggregate_sha256, prompt_contract_id) tuples and that models outside the allowlist run cold.
- It says the new 4-bit checkpoints use new cache namespaces, with old files aging out via the TTL sweep.
- It says logprobs are gated by catalog listing and provider version.

These are descriptions, not implementations. I cannot verify the underlying code from the supplied evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), and the head range (11-246) is largely unseen. Base-side changed lines 11-13 are not among the supplied base units, which start at 1629. No regression, new attack surface, or invalidated assumption can be established from a changelog alone.

Remaining integration questions for later passes that see code: whether the 4-bit checkpoint namespaces keep the HMAC lookup tag, scope folding and 30-minute TTL unchanged (T-041 detection_hint); whether logprob output from cached 4-bit state leaks across scopes; and whether the provider-version gate is enforced. The threat model may need an update if the SSD checkpoint format or its precision or namespace changed in code. That is not demonstrable here.
